sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: One figure: how many products Contoso's catalogue holds — 2,517 — counting each SKU once, where a colour is part of what makes a product its own product, over the product register as the warehouse holds it. What it does NOT include: it is not 888, which is what you get if the 16 colours of one named model are treated as variants of a single product; it is not a count of currently saleable or in-stock goods, because a product row carries no status, discontinuation or availability column at all; and it is not restricted to products that ever sold, since nothing here touches the sales lines.

value: All 2,517 rows of contoso_served.dim_product — every product on record, with no restriction applied. No active/available filter, because the relation serves no status, discontinued, archived or validity column that could express one; no category, price or channel filter; and no join to sales, so products that never sold are counted. Each row counts as one product at the declared SKU grain, colour included, per the Product definition ("at the level the shelf knows it: a SKU") and the Color declaration that "E400 Green" and "E400 Orange" are two products.

value.means: The things to be counted: one row per product in Contoso's catalogue, 2,517 of them, each a distinct SKU whose colour is part of what makes it its own product. turns.why: Get the row set's size and price both readings of "products" at once: product rows/SKUs as stored, against distinct product names with the trailing colour word stripped off, which is the only coarser "one product, many variants" grain this relation could support.
turns.did:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS product_rows,
  COUNT(DISTINCT product_key) AS distinct_product_keys,
  COUNT(DISTINCT product_code) AS distinct_product_codes,
  COUNT(DISTINCT product_name) AS distinct_product_names,
  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN product_name LIKE '%' || color
      THEN RTRIM(LEFT(product_name, LENGTH(product_name) - LENGTH(color)))
      ELSE product_name
    END
  ) AS distinct_names_colour_stripped,
  COUNT(DISTINCT color) AS distinct_colours
FROM contoso_served.dim_product
